text:
jia: Heads-up — ran into a reproducible crash when our Python SDK is imported inside a multiprocessing child (spawn start method). Child process throws RuntimeError: There is no current event loop and then exits.

matt: ugh. which Python + uvloop? spawn is usually Windows/macOS default, right? repro on Linux with spawn too?

jia: linux, python 3.11, no uvloop in the env. I only see it when using spawn (not fork). Quick trace:

jia: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "worker.py", line 28, in <module>
    client = RedwoodClient()
  File "/opt/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
    from .async_client import AsyncClient  # triggers event loop policy setup
  File "/opt/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 40, in <module>
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
RuntimeError: There is no current event loop
```

olivia: hmm looks like an import-time call to asyncio.get_event_loop() — spawn children don't have an event loop set by default. We shouldn't call that at import time.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro? we should add a quick test for spawn/forkserver too.

jia: minimal shown below — create a worker that imports SDK at module top and starts Process:

jia: ```python
# worker.py
from multiprocessing import Process, set_start_method
set_start_method('spawn')
from redwood import AsyncClient  # <-- import-time problem

def child_main():
    c = AsyncClient()
    print('ok')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    p = Process(target=child_main)
    p.start()
    p.join()
```

matt: thanks. quick workaround: defer import into child_main or ensure SDK doesn't touch asyncio at import time. but we should fix upstream.

olivia: I looked — our async_client module sets a default loop policy and calls get_event_loop() to configure per-thread context on import. That's a bad pattern.

jia: I can file an issue + draft PR. proposed change: remove get_event_loop() at import, lazily create loop-aware state inside AsyncClient.__init__ or on first async call. Also add a test that runs under spawn/forkserver.

sam: also add CI job that runs a tiny spawn-based test on linux to catch regressions (flaky but fast).

ci-bot: New issue created: REDWOOD-4872 (python-sdk: avoid import-time asyncio.get_event_loop() to support multiprocessing spawn)

matt: perfect. could we also make the import-time path tolerant: wrap get_event_loop in try/except and fall back to None instead of exploding? less risky for patch release.

olivia: agree — two-step: quick patch (try/except) for patch release, then refactor for proper lazy-init.

jia: I'll open two PRs: one small hotfix branch + follow-up refactor. Will include the minimal repro as a test. assigning to @matt for review.

sam: thanks! leaving a note for docs: call out "avoid importing SDK at top-level of multiprocessing spawn children" until patch lands.

matt: FYI I reproduced locally, hotfix branch passes our new test. Will push review comments shortly.

jia: awesome, thanks 🙏

ci-bot: CI pipeline passed for hotfix/REDWOOD-4872 (linux, py311)

matt: merging hotfix in 5m. After merge I'll open a follow-up to remove the try/except and move to lazy init.

jia: sending a small sample app snippet to the docs PR after merge so onboarding guides mention the fix.

olivia: adding regression note to release checklist.

sam: closing loop — thanks everyone :)
